scope: Botanical review for the ten PNW roadmap species; proposed values for main-agent integration, not automatic catalog imports.

conventions.units: heightIn, spread, space and all dimension evidence use real inches, never renderer pixels.
conventions.heightIn: Representative cultivated overall height, including flowering stems where applicable; not the largest wild specimen.
conventions.space: Suggested on-center garden spacing. Unless explicitly attributed, a design estimate based on crown size, not a measured botanical trait.
conventions.grow: Woody-only planning horizon in years to the stated design size; not root establishment time, lifespan, or a guarantee of maximum maturity.
conventions.zones: Conservative USDA cultivation ranges. Hardiness alone does not establish heat, humidity, summer-water, local-native, or legal suitability.
conventions.bloomMonths: Approximate regional flowering window; flowering varies with elevation and year. Update the canonical bloom-month table during integration. Ferns have no flowers.
conventions.persistence: Biological information for authoring seasonal colors and descriptions; this artifact does not authorize changing seasonal infrastructure.
conventions.taxonomy: Species-level records, no cultivar expansion. Empty synonyms means none recommended for catalog discovery, not an exhaustive taxonomic statement.
conventions.limits: No Phase 0 climate, native-origin, legal-filter, or seasonal-engine changes. All ten species use nativeTo north-america and provenance species under the existing contract. Do not infer deer or rabbit ratings from this review.

evidence.dimensions: Hardy Fern Foundation gives 36–60 in and a large height/spread category exceeding 36 in in five years. OSU describes 12–48 in fronds; frond length is not upright height. Proposed 48-in crown is representative.
evidence.foliageVsFlower: All displayed height is fronds; sori/spores are not blooms. No flower calendar entry.
evidence.hardiness: Direct horticultural range 6–9 from Hardy Fern Foundation. OSU gives a colder minimum of 4; conservative range avoids promising that all stock behaves identically.
evidence.persistence: Evergreen perennial fern, dense crown with renewing spring fronds; no woody grow field.
evidence.spacingConfidence: Moderate design estimate: 36-in spacing allows neighboring mature arching fronds to overlap.

evidence.dimensions: USDA Willamette germplasm flowering stems average 28–45 in; basal crown width is only 4–7 in. UW species account gives overall 35–100 cm (about 14–39 in). Proposed spread is the foliage envelope, not the basal crown.
evidence.foliageVsFlower: Fine basal leaves sit below upright airy flowering stems. A 12–18-in foliage mound is an authoring estimate, not a verified separate foliage-height range.
evidence.hardiness: Yamhill SWCD lists USDA4–9; 6–9 is a deliberately cautious range for this maritime representation. Cold tolerance and growth form depend on seed source; no controlled hardiness trial was found.
evidence.persistence: Long-lived cool-season perennial bunchgrass, without running rhizomes; Yamhill reports potential lifespan to 20 years. Flowering/seed stems turn straw-colored.
evidence.spacingConfidence: Weak-to-moderate numerical evidence for garden envelope and on-center distance. USDA 12–14-in seed-production row spacing is not a garden spacing rule.

evidence.dimensions: OSU gives 96–120-in height; NCSU gives 60–144 in tall and wide. Proposed 120 by 120 in represents a substantial untrimmed species shrub, not a compact cultivar.
evidence.foliageVsFlower: Pendant flower racemes appear on woody branches in early spring around leaf emergence, not on a separate tall flowering stalk.
evidence.hardiness: NCSU explicitly lists USDA6–8; OSU minimum6 agrees.
evidence.persistence: Deciduous perennial woody shrub with arching multiple stems; blue-black fruit follows flowering.
evidence.growConfidence: Moderate estimate of eight years within RHS 5–10-year maturity interval; site, starting size and pruning alter growth.
evidence.spacingConfidence: Design estimate matching the selected untrimmed crown diameter.

evidence.dimensions: OSU ecology account: clumps about 12–16 in across, leaves to 16 in, flowering stems to 14 in. A local seed-growing nursery reports older clumps to 30 in across; proposed24-in garden spread allows expansion.
evidence.foliageVsFlower: Leaves can be longer than the flowering stems. Narrow fans and visible purple iris flowers, not a tall flower spike over tiny foliage.
evidence.hardiness: Yamhill SWCD directly lists USDA6–9. More extreme nursery or UK ratings are not used.
evidence.persistence: Rhizomatous herbaceous perennial; local Oregon seed-grown material is winter deciduous and can lose foliage in severe summer drought. Some horticultural references label it evergreen, so persistence is climate-dependent.
evidence.spacingConfidence: Moderate garden estimate; 18 in is wider than the smaller wild clumps but permits older garden clumps to overlap.

evidence.dimensions: OSU describes variable low cushions through plants about24 in high; Ask Extension gives cultivated spread20–24 in. The24-in proposed height represents a taller local form, not every geographic variety.
evidence.foliageVsFlower: Low green/gray woolly foliage under branching yellow daisies; exact foliage-only height was not established. Avoid an Echinacea-like raised cone even if reusing a daisy renderer.
evidence.hardiness: OSU Garden Ecology Lab gives species-level USDA5–10; proposed6–9 is conservative. Variety-specific hardiness and dimensions were not verified.
evidence.persistence: Herbaceous perennial with a persistent crown and sometimes woody base; longevity and leaf retention vary with site. Do not promise a fixed lifespan or year-round foliage.
evidence.spacingConfidence: Moderate design estimate matching cultivated spread; OSU/NRCS hedgerow guidance uses a wider36-in spacing for larger planting systems.

evidence.dimensions: Great Plant Picks provides an explicit ten-year size of24 by48 in and an eventual mature size of36 by72 in. Proposed fields intentionally use its ten-year design horizon; do not present48 in as an absolute colony limit.
evidence.foliageVsFlower: Long compound evergreen leaves and upright yellow racemes; OSU gives April–June flowers. Flowers sit over the low woody framework rather than forming a tall separate perennial stem.
evidence.hardiness: Great Plant Picks USDA6–9; OSU gives minimum5. Proposed range is the directly documented conservative range.
evidence.persistence: Evergreen woody, slowly stoloniferous shrub; can bronze/purple in winter and sun.
evidence.growConfidence: High for matching an explicitly cited ten-year reference size; not a claim that the colony stops at ten years.
evidence.spacingConfidence: Design estimate matching ten-year width; retain room for later colony expansion.

evidence.dimensions: OSU commonly120–240 in high; NCSU120–300 in high and180–240 in broad. OSU EC1438 gives240-in crown spread. Proposed20-ft tree fits a substantial garden crown, not every old wild maximum.
